content_voiceover: This slide details the treatment schema for intermediate and high risk infant ALL under the TPOG-Infant ALL-2022 protocol. Treatment starts with four weeks of induction containing venetoclax, followed by a fifteen day course of blinatumomab, the first of two planned blinatumomab courses. Then comes ten weeks of early consolidation, after which MRD is checked at time point TP4. That result determines whether the patient is intermediate risk or high risk going forward, but both groups then receive a second fifteen day course of blinatumomab, followed by three weeks of venetoclax reinduction and six weeks of late consolidation. From there, the two risk groups diverge slightly in maintenance: intermediate risk patients receive maintenance A for four weeks times five cycles, while high risk patients instead receive a venetoclax containing maintenance for the same duration; both groups then converge onto maintenance B and maintenance C. Notably, if MRD is positive at the TP4 branch point, the patient is diverted to a three week venetoclax reinduction followed by options for second line therapy, with a further MRD check determining whether the patient proceeds to CAR-T, if MRD is positive, or HSCT, if MRD is negative. The bottom of the slide reinforces the HSCT indications: persistent MRD of 0.01 percent or higher after early consolidation at TP4 warrants transplant after reinduction, and any MRD recurrence during maintenance also warrants transplant once a negative MRD status is re-achieved with salvage therapy. The timeline at the bottom shows MRD is checked at six time points, TP1 through TP6, then every three to four months thereafter.
keypoints: Induction-Ve for four weeks, then blinatumomab I for fifteen days, then early consolidation
MRD at TP4 splits patients into IR or HR pathways, both get blinatumomab II
Positive MRD at the TP4 branch triggers reinduction, second-line options, then CAR-T or HSCT by MRD result
HSCT is indicated for persistent MRD 0.01 percent or higher after early consolidation
HSCT is also indicated for any MRD recurrence during maintenance, after achieving MRD negativity with salvage
keypoint_voiceover: In summary, infants get induction with venetoclax, blinatumomab course one, then early consolidation, with MRD checked at TP4 to assign intermediate or high risk, and both groups then receive a second blinatumomab course. If that MRD branch is positive instead, patients get reinduction and second line options, heading to CAR-T if MRD stays positive or HSCT if it clears. Overall, transplant is indicated for persistent MRD of 0.01 percent or more after early consolidation, or for any MRD recurrence during maintenance once salvage therapy restores MRD negativity.
